summary.text: A 54-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 1-day history of fever and nonproductive cough. On presentation he was afebrile with heart rate 88 beats/min, respiratory rate 16/min, blood pressure 154/96 mmHg and normal arterial oxygen saturation of 98% on room air, with coarse crackles in the bilateral lower lung fields.

The electrocardiogram on admission showed normal sinus rhythm and chest X-ray showed bilateral patchy infiltration. SARS-CoV-2 fluorescence PCR was positive. He was treated with oral amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, azithromycin, hydroxychloroquine, paracetamol and subcutaneous enoxaparin; his fever subsided and symptoms improved on the second day of admission.

On admission day 5 he became hypoxic with oxygen saturation below 90% and received non-rebreather mask oxygen, increased to 10 l/min. On day 8 he suddenly developed profound hypotension and severe desaturation requiring urgent endotracheal intubation. Bedside transthoracic echocardiography revealed large transient thrombi in the right atrium and right ventricle with McConnell’s sign and severe RV failure.
He received fibrinolytic therapy with alteplase 100 mg without significant improvement while preparations were underway for VA-ECMO. He then had a cardiac arrest and subsequently passed away.
